claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is compliant despite a known model-card weakness in the health-plan benefits support segment, based on aggregate readiness, a 3% rollout, rollback capability, monitoring, and asserted disclosure of the limitation.
decision_criteria: Compliant certification requires admissible evidence that the material weakness was either removed from exposed use cases or covered by reviewed risk acceptance.
If certification instead relies on disclosure, the disclosure must be evidenced in the actual model card or release record, not inferred from general guidance.
Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and monitoring controls are supportive context but do not satisfy the missing policy predicate on their own.
When a known below-target segment remains exposed and the required support link is missing, the proportional verdict is suspicious rather than compliant.
evidence_requests: The exact released model-card text showing explicit disclosure of the health-plan benefits support limitation.
Release record or approval artifact showing reviewed risk acceptance for exposing the affected use case, if exclusion was not implemented.
Cohort definition or gating evidence proving the affected use case was excluded, if that is the asserted basis instead of risk acceptance.
Approval chain or sign-off demonstrating policy review of the mitigation basis for launch.
specific_concerns: The policy requires either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance when rollout controls are used to mitigate a material model-card weakness, and the actor summary says neither is shown.
The actor summary says the health-plan benefits support segment remains exposed in the initial cohort.

The actor's narrow certification rationale depends on explicit model-card disclosure of the limitation, but no admissible evidence is provided that such disclosure actually exists in the released model card or release record.
Rollout percentage, dashboarding, and rollback readiness are described, but the policy explicitly says those do not remove disclosure duties by themselves.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record.
That rollout controls and monitoring are sufficient to mitigate the weakness under policy.
That the affected use case was excluded from exposure.
That approved risk acceptance covered the exposed health-plan benefits support use case before launch.
That the required limitation disclosure is actually present in the model card or release record.
